explanation: In Mendel's monohybrid crosses, self-pollination of the F1 generation produces the F2 generation, resulting in a predictable 3:1 ratio of dominant to recessive phenotypes.

questions.q: What is the expected phenotypic ratio of dominant to recessive traits in the F2 generation of a monohybrid cross?
questions.exp: Option B is correct because the selfing of heterozygotes in a monohybrid cross results in a 3:1 phenotypic ratio (three dominant to one recessive).
